blocks.text: Setting up your Notion workspace for creative work

Start by installing the native Notion desktop app. It runs better on macOS than a browser tab. Open the Notion menu in the top bar to check for updates regularly. Use the ⌘ + N shortcut to open a new window when you need to view your content calendar and a client brief side by side.

Speed is vital when you are in a writing flow. Typing / opens the block menu. You can then type header to pick an H1, H2, or H3. Use ⌘ + Shift + 7 to create a numbered list. Use ⌘ + Shift + 8 for a bulleted list. If you need to find a specific page, press ⌘ + P to open the quick search. This saves you from clicking through the sidebar folders.

blocks.text: A database is the heart of a copywriter's workflow. Use a table view to see project status, deadlines, and word counts. Create a property for Status with options like To Do, Drafting, Editing, and Done. You can then filter this view to show only your active tasks. This keeps your workspace focused on the work that matters today.
How Lazur helps you write faster in Notion

Lazur lives in your Mac notch. It sees your screen and hears your voice. When you are stuck on a headline, hold the fn key and dictate your ideas. Lazur types clean text directly into your Notion page. If you are struggling with a complex database filter, hold ⌥ + ⌘ and ask Lazur where to find the filter menu. It will circle the button for you.

items: Over-nesting pages: It makes finding content harder. Use databases instead of deep folder structures.
Ignoring templates: Create a template for your client briefs. You will save time on every new project.
Not using search: Relying on the sidebar to find files is slow. Use ⌘ + P every time.
Cluttering the page: Use toggles to hide long research notes so your draft stays clean.

blocks.text: Copywriting requires long periods of deep work. Turn on Focus mode in macOS settings to silence notifications from Slack or email. Use the Notion desktop app in full screen by pressing ⌃ + ⌘ + F. This removes the distraction of other open windows. If you need to research a topic, use Lazur to run a search in the background. It will bring back a summary while you continue writing your draft.

Every writer needs a place for inspiration. Create a gallery view database for your swipe files. Add a tag property to categorize them by industry, tone, or format. When you find a great ad or email, use the Notion Web Clipper to save it to your gallery. This makes it easy to find examples when you start a new project.
Using templates to scale your output

Templates are the secret to consistency. Create a standard structure for your blog posts. Include sections for the working title, target audience, keyword research, and the draft itself. When you start a new post, click the arrow next to the New button in your database and select your template. It populates the page with all your required sections in one click.

faq.question: Can Lazur edit my Notion pages directly?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons or edit files for you. It can dictate text at your cursor or point at UI elements to guide you.

faq.question: Does Notion work on older Macs?
faq.answer: Notion requires macOS 13 or later. Check your macOS version in the Apple menu > About This Mac.

faq.question: How do I find shortcuts in Notion?
faq.answer: Press Shift + ? on your keyboard to see the full list of Notion shortcuts.

faq.question: Is my data safe when using Lazur?
faq.answer: Yes. Lazur only sees your screen and listens while you hold the shortcut key. Data is not stored or used to train AI models.
